_comment: T-45C Goshawk VALIDATION CASE for the turbofan sizing code. The aim is to reproduce a real, single-engine, carrier-capable jet trainer, so you can see how close the models come before you use them on a new design. Every value says where it came from: 'NAVY FACT FILE' = US Navy fact file 'T-45A Goshawk Training Aircraft' (navy.mil, updated Oct 2021; all T-45As have been converted to T-45C), 'P-1231' = CNATRA P-1231 T-45 Aerodynamics Student Workbook, Appendix A 'T-45 Aeronautical Data' (Navy, July 1999), 'ENGINE (SECONDARY)' = published Adour Mk 871 / F405 figures that are NOT from Rolls-Royce or the Navy, 'PLACEHOLDER' = no public source; a textbook or engineering estimate you should replace with NATOPS or course data if you have it. Keys that start with an underscore are documentation only.
_the_real_airplane: NAVY FACT FILE: 1 x F405-RR-401, 5,527 lbf; empty weight 9,394 lb; max takeoff weight 13,500 lb; span 30 ft 10 in; length 39 ft 4 in; max speed 645 mph (about 560 kt); ceiling 42,500 ft; range 700 nmi; crew 2. P-1231: wing area 179.64 ft^2; 75.4 psf clean with 2,904 lb fuel (so about 13,545 lb); zero-fuel weight 10,332-10,400 lb. Installed thrust at 5 % installation loss: 5,527 x 0.95 = 5,251 lbf, so the real airplane sits at W/S = 13,500/179.64 = 75.2 psf and (T/W)_installed = 5,251/13,500 = 0.389 - that is the design_point below.

geometry._comment: SHAPE only; S_ref is written by the loop. Wing data from P-1231 Appendix A.
geometry._src_AR: P-1231 Appendix A: AR 5.0. NOTE the source is not self-consistent: the fact-file span (30.83 ft) with P-1231's 179.64 ft^2 gives AR 5.29, and AR 5.0 with that span needs about 190 ft^2 (the area several secondary sources quote). Probably different reference-area definitions. P-1231's AR and area are used together here, so the modelled span is 29.97 ft, 0.9 ft short of the real one.
geometry._src_sweep_quarter_chord_deg: P-1231 Appendix A (leading edge 28.67 deg; TfGeom computes 28.5 deg from AR, taper and this value, so it is below 30 deg and TfAero uses Raymer's straight-wing Oswald formula, Eq. 12.48).
geometry._src_twist_incidence_dihedral: P-1231 Appendix A (2.67 deg washout, 2 deg dihedral). Incidence not published. Reporting only - not read by the sizing loop.

horizontal_tail._src: Volume coefficient: Raymer Table 6.4, jet trainer c_HT = 0.70. Sweep: P-1231 (stabilator, 30.14 deg quarter chord, 10 deg anhedral). Arm, AR, taper and t/c are PLACEHOLDERS (tail areas and arms are not published) - an arm of 15 ft is a scale estimate off the 39.3 ft length; it gives S_ht of about 52 ft^2.

vertical_tail._src: Volume coefficient: Raymer Table 6.4, jet trainer c_VT = 0.06. Everything else PLACEHOLDER (scale estimates); gives S_vt of about 23 ft^2.

fuselage._comment: Constant through the loop. PLACEHOLDER dimensions: tandem two-seat cockpit, engine and intakes inside the fuselage. Total 38.5 ft of fuselage inside the 39.3 ft overall length (the nose probe and tail account for the rest). Width includes the intake fairings.
fuselage._src_lengths: PLACEHOLDER scale estimates. Measure them off a three-view if you have one: the fuselage is the largest wetted area, so it drives CD0.

nacelle._comment: The T-45's single engine is BURIED in the fuselage, so there is no separate nacelle: installation = 'buried' makes the nacelle wetted area zero. The two factors are kept because TfGeom still reads them (they only affect the reported nacelle size).
nacelle._src: Layout of the real airplane (engine in the centre fuselage, intakes either side of the cockpit).

landing_gear._src: PLACEHOLDER Raymer Ch. 11 ratios. Used only by landing_gear_loads, after the loop.

aerodynamics._comment: No T-45 drag polar or CLmax is public (they are in the distribution-limited NATOPS manual). Textbook values for the class are used.
aerodynamics._src_Cfe: Raymer Table 12.3, Navy fighter: Cfe = 0.0040 (Air Force fighter 0.0035). PLACEHOLDER for a carrier-capable trainer with its tail hook, heavy gear and fixed probe.
aerodynamics._src_CD0_reference: CHECK VALUE only: typical clean CD0 of a jet trainer of this class.
aerodynamics._src_airfoil_type: The T-45 wing is a conventional section (not supercritical). Options: 'supercritical' (Korn kappa_A 0.95: flat-topped, aft-loaded section) or 'conventional' (0.87: NACA 6-series style). 'custom' uses korn_technology_factor instead. The type only moves the Korn drag-divergence Mach in this model; handling effects are not modelled. Override per run with run_tf_constraints/run_tf_sizing(..., 'airfoil', 'conventional') or trade it with airfoil_sweep_study.
aerodynamics._src_CLmax_reference_sweep_deg: The quarter-chord sweep the three CLmax values above are quoted at. TfAero scales all three by cos(sweep)/cos(this) when geometry.sweep_quarter_chord_deg differs (Raymer Sec. 12.4), so a sweep change also costs CLmax. Remove the key to use CLmax as given at any sweep.
aerodynamics._src_CLmax: PLACEHOLDERS. Roskam Part I Table 3.1, military trainers: clean 1.2-1.8, takeoff 1.4-2.0, landing 1.6-2.2. The T-45 has leading-edge slats and double-slotted flaps; NATOPS stall speeds would let you back these out exactly.
aerodynamics._src_increments: Roskam Part I Table 3.6 low end-to-middle values. PLACEHOLDERS.
aerodynamics._src_delta_CD0_windmilling_engine: Not used: a single-engine airplane has no engine-out condition.

propulsion._comment: Rolls-Royce F405-RR-401 (Adour Mk 871 family), low bypass, no afterburner, so the low-bypass DRY models. T_SL is the INSTALLED SLS thrust; the code divides by (1 - installation loss) to get the catalogue figure, and the engine regressions are calibrated at the catalogue figure of 5,527 lbf.
propulsion._src_n_engines: NAVY FACT FILE: one engine. No condition below may set oei = true (TfProp stops with an error if one does).
propulsion._src_bypass_ratio: ENGINE (SECONDARY): Adour family about 0.75-0.8 (Wikipedia, Rolls-Royce Turbomeca Adour).
propulsion._src_lapse_model: Mattingly AED 2nd ed. Eq. 2.54b at military (dry) power, normalised to 1 at SLS. No F405 lapse data is public.
propulsion._src_throttle_ratio: PLACEHOLDER. Mattingly suggests about 1.0-1.08 for a low-bypass engine. It matters a lot at the sea-level max-speed condition (M 0.84 has theta_0 = 1.14, above TR): try 1.00 and 1.08 to see the effect.
propulsion._src_tsfc_scale: ENGINE (SECONDARY): Adour dry SLS TSFC about 0.81 lb/(lbf hr) (Wikipedia). Mattingly Eq. 3.55b gives 0.90 at SLS, so the correlation is scaled by 0.81/0.90 = 0.90; it keeps its Mach and altitude trends.
propulsion._src_T_TO_over_T_max_continuous: PLACEHOLDER. No condition below uses the max-continuous rating.
propulsion._src_installation_loss_fraction: PLACEHOLDER: 5 % for intake ducts and bleed/power extraction. The fact-file 5,527 lbf is taken as the UNINSTALLED rating.
propulsion._src_design_mach: About the maximum level-flight Mach (NAVY FACT FILE 645 mph at sea level is M 0.85). Enters the engine-length regression.
propulsion._src_engine_regression: Raymer Eqs. 10.1-10.3 with the COEFFICIENTS CALIBRATED so that 5,527 lbf at BPR 0.78 and M 0.85 reproduces the Adour Mk 871 (ENGINE (SECONDARY), Deagel: dry weight 589 kg = 1,299 lb, length 1.96 m = 6.43 ft, fan diameter 0.57 m = 1.87 ft). Raymer's own coefficients (0.084, 0.185, 0.033) give 1,061 lb, 5.62 ft and 2.53 ft - 18 % light, 13 % short and 35 % too wide for this engine. The exponents are Raymer's, so the engine still scales like a rubber engine if the loop resizes it.

fixed_engine.name: F405-RR-401 (Adour reference)
fixed_engine._src: Uses the existing T-45 JSON reference thrust, engine weight and dimensions. The existing 5% installation loss is retained; installed thrust is 5250.65 lbf.

weights._comment: Raymer Table 15.2 FIGHTER column (the closest of the three to a carrier-capable jet trainer), with the Navy landing-gear fraction, then the all-else-empty fraction CALIBRATED so the build-up reproduces the real 9,394 lb empty weight at the real airplane's size (13,500 lb, 179.64 ft^2, 5,527 lbf). See the T-45C section of README.md for the calibration run.
weights._src_W_payload: Crew and operating items = zero-fuel weight (P-1231, 10,332 lb) minus empty weight (NAVY FACT FILE, 9,394 lb) = 938 lb. Two crew with flight gear account for about 500 lb of it.
weights._src_unit_weights: Raymer Table 15.2, fighter column: wing 9.0 psf exposed, horizontal tail 4.0, vertical tail 5.3, fuselage 4.8 psf wetted.
weights._src_landing_gear_fraction: Raymer Table 15.2: 0.033 W0 for a fighter, 0.045 W0 for a NAVY (carrier) fighter. The T-45 has a carrier gear.
weights._src_installed_engine_factor: Raymer Table 15.2 fighter column: 1.3 x bare engine.
weights._src_all_else_empty_fraction: CALIBRATED to the 9,394 lb empty weight: at 13,500 lb, 179.64 ft^2 and 5,527 lbf the other six rows add up to 6,314 lb, so all-else = (9,394 - 6,314)/13,500 = 0.228. That is 34 % above Raymer's fighter value (0.17); it absorbs the carrier structure (catapult and arresting loads), which Raymer's land-based unit weights do not include, and every placeholder in the geometry. Re-run the calibration if you change any geometry or unit weight.
weights._src_statistical_empty: Raymer Table 3.1, jet trainer: We/W0 = 1.59 W0^-0.10. CROSS-CHECK ONLY. At 13,500 lb it predicts about 8,300 lb, 12 % under the real T-45C: the carrier structure makes it heavier than the land-based trainers in Raymer's fit.
weights._src_fuel_density: JP-5, about 6.8 lb/US gal. Post-sizing wing-volume check only. The T-45 carries most of its fuel in fuselage tanks, so a 'short' wing-fuel result is expected.

constraints._comment: NOT FAR 25. A single-engine Navy trainer has no engine-out climb requirements; it is sized by carrier approach, wave-off, field takeoff and its published flight performance. Where the fact file gives a performance figure (max speed, ceiling) it is used AS a requirement, so the real airplane should sit close to those curves - that checks the aerodynamics and the engine lapse. Catapult launch is NOT modelled (it needs the catapult end-speed and wind-over-deck, which are not public).
constraints._condition_keys: type: takeoff | landing | approach_speed | climb_gradient | flight. See get_con for the optional keys and defaults.
constraints._src_W_TO_estimate_lbf: NAVY FACT FILE maximum takeoff weight.

design_point._src: THE REAL AIRPLANE: 13,500 lb / 179.64 ft^2 = 75.2 psf; 5,527 lbf x 0.95 installed / 13,500 lb = 0.389.

conditions.name: Field takeoff
conditions._src: PLACEHOLDER requirement (no public T-45 field length). Uses Roskam's FAR 25 field-length correlation, s = 37.5 TOP25, as an approximation: that correlation includes an engine failure at V1, which a single-engine airplane does not have, so it is CONSERVATIVE here.

conditions.name: Carrier approach speed
conditions._src: PLACEHOLDER 125 KEAS maximum approach speed (replace with the NATOPS on-speed approach speed or your requirement). k = 1.15: Raymer Sec. 5.3, Navy carrier approach speed = 1.15 x power-approach stall speed. beta 0.85 = maximum arrested-landing weight / W_TO, PLACEHOLDER.

conditions.name: Wave-off climb
conditions._src: PLACEHOLDER: about 500 ft/min rate of climb at the approach speed (500 ft/min / 211 ft/s = 4 % gradient), landing configuration, full military thrust, at landing weight. Engine spool-up time, which really drives a wave-off, is not modelled.

conditions.name: Max speed 560 kt SL
conditions._src: NAVY FACT FILE: 645 mph = 560 kt; taken at sea level, which is M 0.84-0.85. Full military thrust. beta 0.90 (mid-sortie weight) is a PLACEHOLDER - the fact file does not give the weight.

conditions.name: Service ceiling 42,500 ft
conditions._src: NAVY FACT FILE: ceiling 42,500 ft, taken as a SERVICE ceiling, 100 ft/min = 1.667 ft/s. M 0.70 and beta 0.85 are PLACEHOLDERS.

std_mission._description: Ferry mission to check the fuel against the fact-file range: start/taxi/takeoff, climb to 35,000 ft, cruise 700 nmi, descent, landing, plus a reserve. PLACEHOLDER profile - the fact file gives only '700 nmi' with no profile or reserves, so expect only rough agreement.
std_mission._src_fixed_fractions: Roskam Part I Table 2.1, military trainers: start 0.990 x taxi 0.995 x takeoff 0.995 = 0.980; descent 0.990; landing/taxi/shutdown 0.995. The real airplane carries 2,904 lb internal fuel (P-1231).

_fixed_analysis_note: Prepared 2026-11-19 for concept_sizing. Wing area and engine fixed; takeoff weight solved. Existing geometry estimates, mission, weight calibration and engine/TSFC assumptions retained. No claim that all geometry was extracted from OpenVSP. Weight closure predicts mission takeoff weight, not structural maximum takeoff weight.
